text: Welcome to the U⚡️Sportz editing tutorial.
Over the next twelve minutes, we'll walk through the full editing flow, step by step: opening the editor, picking a filter, adding custom animations, and finishing with trimming and music.
Grab one of your highlight reels, and let's build a better edit together.
Here's U⚡️Sportz, the platform built for the next generation of athletes and creators.
Highlights, editing, podcasts, live streams and community, all in one place.
This first screen is a real capture of the app.
Everything we cover today happens inside the video editor, which you reach from your own highlight reels.
This is the in-app editing guide.
It breaks the whole process into four steps.
One, open the editor.
Two, pick a filter.
Three, add custom animations.
Four, trim and add music.
We'll take each step in order, and spend real time on the choices that make a highlight feel finished.
A quick note before we start.
Some screens in this tutorial are illustrated mock-ups, drawn in code to explain each control clearly.
They're based on the in-app guide and the editor's actual options, but they are not screen recordings.
Whenever you see the illustration tag in the corner, that's what you're looking at.
Open the editor.
Start with any of your highlight reels.
On the reel, look for the Edit / Filters button, marked with the sparkle icon.
Tap it, and the full-screen editor opens with your video already loaded.
There's nothing to import and nothing to set up.
Your clip is ready to work on right away.
Once the editor is open, your video sits in the large preview area.
Along the side is the toolbar, where each tool lives in its own tab: Filters, Adjust, Effects, Transitions, Music, Text, Stickers and Trim.
Today we'll focus on four of them, Filters, the FX plus animations, Trim, and Music.
The preview is your best friend: every change you make shows up there.
Pick a filter.
Tap Filters in the side toolbar.
You'll see the full set of looks: Original, Vintage, Cool, Warm, Vivid, Noir, Neon, Fade, Dreamy, Cinematic, Retro and Pop.
Original is always there as your starting point, so you can compare any look against the untouched clip, or go back to it at any time.
The preview updates live.
Tap a filter, and the clip changes instantly, so you can audition looks one after another without waiting.
On screen now, we're applying the same color recipes the editor uses to a sample frame, cycling through each look, so you can see how much the mood of a single moment can shift.
Vintage adds a warm sepia tone with extra contrast.
It's great for throwback moments, career recaps, or anything that should feel like a memory.
Warm pushes saturation and shifts the hue toward golden tones, a natural fit for outdoor games, sunsets, and summer tournaments.
Cool goes the other way, with stronger saturation and a shift toward blues.
It suits indoor courts, rinks, and pools.
Vivid doubles the saturation and lifts contrast, so jerseys and court lines really pop.
Neon goes even further, with heavy saturation and extra brightness, for a bold, high-energy look.
Noir turns the clip fully black and white with strong contrast.
It's dramatic, and it focuses attention on movement and form rather than color.
Dreamy adds a very soft blur with lifted brightness, for slow, reflective moments, like a walk-off, a celebration, or a post-game hug.
A few tips for choosing a filter.
Match the look to the moment, not just to your taste.
Keep it consistent across a series of clips, so your profile feels like one story.
And always check the faces and the ball in the preview.
If either gets lost, try a gentler look, or go back to Original.
Here's an example still from a U⚡️Sportz timeline export.
On the left, the original moment.
On the right, the same moment with a title and a timed rim effect added.
Small touches like these guide the viewer's eye to exactly what matters in the play.
Step three.
Add custom animations.
Tap FX+ to open the effects panel.
Inside, you'll find two collections: Sport Animations and Character Transforms.
Sport Animations are built around big moments in a game.
Character Transforms restyle a player into a themed character look.
Sport Animations are sorted by sport: Basketball, Football, Soccer, Baseball, Tennis, Hockey, Track, and Swimming, plus an All view.
In basketball, for example, you'll find Swish, Dunk Slam, 3-Pointer, and Crossover.
In soccer, there's Goal, Keeper Save, Free Kick, and Bicycle Kick.
Pick the one that matches the play you captured.
Every effect is clearly badged as either Free or PRO.
In basketball, Swish and Dunk Slam carry the Free badge, while 3-Pointer and Crossover carry the PRO badge.
The badge tells you which tier an effect belongs to before you choose it.
For details about PRO, check the information shown inside the app.
Character Transforms are grouped into themes, including anime, cartoon, superhero, and athlete styles.
A few examples: Ninja Mode, Speedster, Basketball Legend, and Speed Demon are marked Free, while Boxing Champion is marked PRO.
Each one is badged the same way as the sport animations.
Character transforms are placed with pins.
You can drop up to two character pins on the video.
Place each pin on the player you want to highlight.
Two is the limit, so choose your stars wisely: usually the player who makes the play, and maybe the teammate who set it up.
Some tips for animations.
Less is more: one well-timed effect on the key moment hits harder than five scattered ones.
Put the effect right where the action peaks.
And pair it with your filter, a Neon look with a high-energy animation, or Noir with a single dramatic pin, for a style that feels intentional.
Step four.
Trim and add music.
Open Trim to set your in and out points.
There are two sliders: Start sets where your clip begins, and End sets where it finishes.
Each shows its time as you drag, and below them, the editor shows the final duration, so you always know exactly how long your edit will be.
Good trimming makes a highlight.
Start just before the action begins, so viewers have a moment to see the setup.
End right after the payoff, the shot dropping, the goal, the celebration.
Cut the dead time on either side.
A tight eight seconds almost always beats a loose thirty.
Now for music.
Open Music, and you can add background music from the library.
Tracks are listed with a title, an artist, a length and a mood, things like Victory Anthem, Champion's Rise, Game Day Energy, or Cool Down.
Pick a mood that matches your filter and the energy of the play.
Prefer your own sound?
You can upload your own track instead.
This is a good spot to bring in a song you've made, or audio you have permission to use.
Your uploaded track works in the edit just like a library track.
Finally, use fade in and fade out.
A fade in brings the music up smoothly instead of starting abruptly, and a fade out lets it settle at the end, rather than cutting off mid-beat.
Short fades of a second or two usually feel the most natural, and make your edit sound polished.
Let's recap the full flow.
One, tap the Edit / Filters button on a highlight reel to open the full-screen editor.
Two, pick a filter, and watch the live preview.
Three, tap FX+ for Sport Animations and Character Transforms, check the Free and PRO badges, and drop up to two character pins.
Four, trim your in and out points, then add library music or upload your own, with a fade in and out.
Before you post, run a quick checklist.
Does the clip start right before the action?
Is the key moment easy to see with your filter?
Is there one clear effect where the play peaks?
Does the music fade in and out cleanly?
If you can answer yes to all four, your highlight is ready.
That's the complete editing walkthrough.
Open the editor on one of your reels and try it now.
